annotations.sys_contextual_flexibility: when a display fails without any sign of trouble, that expectation has to bend
Once the display itself broke down invisibly, the reason for that verification requirement disappears
when the very tool meant to inform that decision fails silently, the case for strict accountability weakens
annotations.pd_harm_distress: I still ache for the loss

annotations.sys_contextual_flexibility: When a system fails without any warning sign, the reason for demanding extra verification no longer applies
When that trust is betrayed by a hidden fault, the standard of 'check everything twice' stops making sense
since nothing signaled trouble, the case for extra scrutiny falls away
when the failure gives no odd signs at all, that duty has nothing to attach to
information was corrupted invisibly, which removes the basis for expecting greater diligence
Without that doubt, the requirement to double-check doesn't really apply
That absence of any warning changes what we can reasonably ask of the operator
